Did they mess up? Yes. Did they mess up big time? Yes. Did they abandon the project due to severely negative feedback? No. While I agree with most of the criticism this game received at launch, I also can't help but feel that it is a common criticism given to other major title releases. *Cough* The Division *Cough* Watch dogs *Cough*

This is a common opinion when something big is released. They were ambitious and I don't think that should be looked down upon. Instead, I think we should look at what they gave us and what they continue to give us, a massive procedurally generated universe that is nearly unparallelled in similar titles, updates that make exploring easier and customization to make the game our own. 

Was this game a flashy, modern title with bells and whisles? No. At its core, this is a game for explorers whos only desire is to continue searching. This may not appeal to many gamers, but there is a zen in its simplistic approach. Don't try to make this game something that it isn't and therefore criticize it. I happily accept what this game is and what the developers were going for. Although they screwed up pretty bad at the beginning, there is heart in the way that they are trying to redeem themselves and that is a game company that cares about their product. I doubt that we will get what was promised, and maybe accepting that makes me an idiot, but I can't deny that I get some enjoyment out of exploring that chief mechanic and theme that this game was meant to show. In the end, it's worth playing, but like all games, never buy it at full price.

Reviews.174681:
For me, NMS has always been a first class gaming experience, the sheer size and beauty of the game is breathtaking - even if it is procgen.  Now, perhaps NMS didn't have enough of a full game loop at launch, or even now, and I would agree that it definitely needs some more work there.  Nor did it quite live up to the hype, be it Sean's hype, or the hype of the gaming press and public at large, and the ending when reaching the centre of the galaxy was most definitely an epic anti-climax of huge proportions and for me the biggest disappointment so far about NMS.

Nor was it the game many had hoped it would be, but for me, that is often the problem of those peoples own expectations, their own due diligence and possibly their own attention span, as for me, it has always been apparent what NMS is and isn't about.  If you were paying attention you would know that the game wasn't going to be a multiplayer experience, but was meant as a solo 'chill' experience.  However, there was and always is potential for it to go down that avenue, and maybe it still will.

Don't let any of that, or the negativity bandwagon that many people have climbed aboard since release (and I've read some preposterous things being said that have been borderline libel in all honesty), railroad you from trying out this beautiful game experience that is only getting better and better with each update, as the last two significant and free updates have proven and it seems there is much more in the pipeline to come.

For me personally, it was worth every penny of the full asking price, I have had a few hundred hours of enjoyment from it since release, and the way things are going I'm sure I'm going to have many more, when its on sale or offer though, I'd say its an absolute no-brainer if you are intrigued from what you have seen of the game yourself on streams / videos and like exploration / discovery.

If you're after a non-stop shooter / multiplayer / realistic space sim, then NMS probably won't be your bag right now.

However, if you like getting yourself immersed in stylised sci-fi / space scenarios and exploring an unimaginably vast universe (albeit procgen but with some amazingly beautiful results - touchdown on a new planet to see what's what is always a thrill for me), and if you like what you see from videos / streams then I'd highly recommend NMS.  I think the tide of hate is slowly turning, and this game is going to continue getting better and better. 

I'm not being fanboi, just being fair.

Reviews.174751:
TL;DR

Game is awesome but still has a lot of things it needs to add.

Empty sandbox mostly, but great for those who wants to play around in a simple futuristic space flying and walking sim.

Full review

This game is pretty cool and even with the newest pathfinder update still shows potential. Although I preordered the game and one for my friend too, we still hold out hope and anticipation of multiplayer being less of an idea and more of a tangible concept. 
I love the exploration and survival aspect, but there is a lot of walking on planets which are in most part empty. Even with freighters added I still find inventory a chore with how little you and your ship can carry. Space battles aren't too bad and getting your ship outfitted to do them isn't too hard either, but like almost all games where you mine minerals for crafting, it gets kind of grindy at times.

Overall the game is pretty good but still unfinished. it gets old after a while doing the same thing again and again, adding different things to do and different ways of doing what's already there would benefit the experience greatly. Like adding more equipment modifications to the char or the ships to help locate ores or pirates. Making your freighter have rotating NPCs that you can hire or an interactive map that can scan sectors for certain points of interest. There's so much this game could add that I can't list all my ideas here, but there are other games out there these guys should learn from. 

Games like this are all about your own experience and being able to customize your experience is what makes or breaks it. The newest update fixes part of this thank goodness. They fell short by not adding all the features from the start, but I still support this company and can't wait to see what else they'll add along the way.

In the little six hours I have played No Man's Sky, I can very safely say this has become of my favorite games. (hear me out) I never really followed this game or the hype that was built around it until the bad reviews started rolling in. At which point I decided to take a closer look at the reviews and what they had to say (lying, lack luster, and just overall a terrible game) blah blah so on.  It wasn't until yesterday, however, I decided to take the time and draw my own conclusions on "The worst game of 2016" or even to go as worst game ever!  I made sure to play a good while before writing this review to get a good understanding of how you do things, and what things there are to do.

Before going any further I will just say right now: If you're looking for an action packed space shoot 'em up, you will be let down!
I was aware of this before buying this game and I personally love games with a heavy emphasis on exploration which you sadly do not see more of. (Jurassic Park: Trespasser)

Off to the review now. When first I entered NMS I was very impressed with the landscape and overall scenery. It felt like I was really on another planet!  Noticing my first goal is to repair my heavily damaged ship, I head off to gather resources where I encountered many creatures both harmless, and hostile. Every creature I faced was unique and this greatly varies from planet to planet, where one may be thriving, while another can be completely baron. HOWEVER! This is not exactly a good thing, as it is so varied that some planets have laughable beasts that cannot be taken seriously and breaks the immersion. Almost like spore creatures made by a young child.. the algorithm for this is a little messy, but most times it makes some very interesting animals!  Which makes venturing out to other worlds very very fun for me.  But the interaction with player and the animals is almost non existent. This being said, this greatly hinders what NMS could be, seeing as interaction is one of the main keys to gameplay.

Moving on to resource gathering and base exploring.
Gathering resources for you or your ship is pretty average I must agree and I could see how this could get reptitive. But it is the way of getting to the materials you need that makes it fun. going in caves, climbing atop a vantage point to get a better view of your surroundings, exploring different parts of the worlds, and sometimes facing a dangerous run in with the beings that inhabit the world you are alien to or shooting down drones. 

Base and ruin exploring is generally the same as resource gathering but you get the satisfying feeling of learning a new word, or obtaining a rare item!

Overall No Man's Sky is a very fun game for what it is and not what it was hyped up to be. If you have the time to explore distant lands and get the enjoyment out of doing so with tidbits of action, this is definately the game for you. 
No Man's Sky has given me a very good memorable gaming experiance that no other game has given me. And for that I can't really complain.

I look forward to future updates on this flawed, yet amazing game

Reviews.174894:
So then, No Man's Sky. Arguably the most controversial game ever relased, and certainly of recent times, the hype over this game led to outrage over the final product.

Thing is, I never knew about any of the hype, I hadn't even heard of the game, or any of the promises. All I did was show up after it was released and play it.

So, this review, rather than pining over what the game isn't, I'm going to review based on what it is.

In short, NMS is an exploration grind for the OCD'r in you, a relaxing stroll through procedurally created planets with their resources, lifeforms, and outposts. Add a bit of space exploration and some basic trading with a hint of a plot about the centre of the universe and Atlas, and a choice between that or pure free exploring, plus some random aliens who give you stuff and either get upset or happy with you based on what you say to them, and that is basically it.

Visually it is average, if not good, at 4K - the SLI scaling could be better and my 980Ti SLI gets about 20-50fps - there are times it looks close to slideshow,  and the pop-up can be irritating. But the Pathfinder, adding that 4K native resolution is always a plus.

The sound is rather good - some quirky alien creature sounds, decent music and the general ambience does lend quite well to an outer spacey atmosphere.

As for the gameplay? The mouselook isn't the best and the ship's controls are clunky, but in terms of what it is, rather than what it was supposedly promised as, it really is good fun and easy to get totally lost in. I just spent 3 hours cataloguing all the outposts and creatures of my starting planet and have only just left. And I found it relaxing, strangely therapeutic, and oddly satisfying.

There's not a lot more, and I know that. But I knew that before I bought it (at half price, definitely not worth the full £40) and that's why I shelled out.

For what it is, I like it a lot. It may well run out of novelty value soon, and I might well find myself bored pretty quickly, but so far it's grabbed my attention and I don't think I'll mind a journey to Atlas or the centre of the universe.

That is said, it IS a unique game - no game like this ever got made before, and it is for a certain kind of person. This is for you 'tro-hos' from Playstation, or those who like all their achievements on Steam - it's for those who like to 'do everything' and be given a shiny notification for it.

All while walking around looking at weird aliens and landscapes.

It's a niche market, but one I like.

EDIT: 13/03/17

So there is WAY more than what I just detailed in this review - with the Pathfinder update base building, ground vehicles, teleportation etc have been added and it's easy to get completely lost in this. One slight issue is the prediliction for 'fetch' gameplay, whereby one task requires something else, which itself needs something else etc. Ubisoft games are infamous for this kind of gameplay - but I can't deny this game is addictive and compelling. It remains as fun now as when I started. Maybe more so.

The release of this game was a hot mess and a total disaster that will probably never be forgotten. There's nothing to say about that part, that hasn't already been said at least 100 times. 

Moving beyond that and looking at the game itself past all the controversy - does it stand up as a decent game at all? I believe it very much does, but that fully depends on what kind of gaming experience you're looking for.

Its not for everyone, so definitely do your own research before deciding if you want to get this game. 

For me, its pretty, relaxing and has that feeling of emptiness and aloneness I look for in a space game. The atmosphere as a whole, is fantastic. I'd say that's where the game succeeds the most. 

I like just wandering around aimlessly in space when the mood hits. I like collecting things and crafting. I like the base building a lot, and I really enjoy the vaguely ominous story when I get in the mood to move forward, and learning bits about the alien races and their lore is fun too.

The last two updates really brought some great additions. It was doubtlessly a little bare-bones on release but I honestly enjoyed it then, too. Its a lot more fleshed out and engaging now. Could it stand to be better? Certainly. I look forward to more updates in the future but I'm still enjoying it now and that's the important part.

If you're looking for something fast paced and action packed, you might need to look elsewhere. Though I will say there are still some panic inducing moments where you can get yourself into trouble, and some much more dangerous modes now, including permadeath - but this is not an action game.  

Ultimately for me, this is one of my favorite late night "chill-out" games and it suits that purpose well.

Most of the viewpoints are in Super Bunnyhop's YT channel (merely a plug if you'd argue so, I'm not much of an advertiser)
His review is pretty clean and remains informative. He's got a talent for writing. Not saying "hey go sub he's cool//fanboy here" but this review is at least worth a watch. My half-ass attempt to "copy/pasta" his review is simply used for guidelines. I watched the review a coupld weeks ago and decided to write my review after giving it some though.


An honest, rant-free review:

Traveling/Exploring

You will like this. Hello games got this formula pretty decent and this feature alone can generate enough wallpapers to launch a website (good ones at that). Your inner "dora the explorer" will be happy. But this feeling will quickly fade away when you experience it on only a handful of planets that inhabit mostly.... hauntingly familiar looking creatures and biomes. Of the 2 options (freelance through the universe or do the "story mode"), neither will differ much in what you're doing.



Grinding/Building/Sand-box

Can't comment much past the foundation patch since I didn't play as much after that but it's still worth mentioning. The grinding, while not as big anymore, is still a problem that shows developers simply have no experience with these types of systems. My biggest complaint, even bigger than the awful launch, would be how crucial inventory space is but how little you get of it. Pre order bonus is a joke; apperantly it has the same number of slots as a starter ship. That said, why give a pre-order bonus when the first thing a player does is get rid of it? 



Social Interaction

The game's alien races lack any form of character. This is old news by now, specially when some people comment on predicting what happens. There was almost no motivation when writing the promts either; either you solved a 5th grader math problem or you guessed an answer that wouldn't change from the last 99 previous times encountered...it was the same question but different "language."


The new updates (and this latest one) will simply, in my mind, be only a band-aid placed on top of the injury caused by releasing an unfinished product. These patches will likely not change what makes the game, THE game, and continue to ignore those vexing little features that slowly diminish what could have been an entertaining exploration sandbox.


TD;LR (I guess)
To put it into perspective, I enjoyed, despite the controversy, the first 2-3 days of the game but then, as the repetitive tasks started to take up most of my playing time, the exciting new planet to discover turned out to be a distant cousin of the last; this also meant that I'd be doing a lot of grinding to fly to the next which didn't justify stopping in a planet in the first place. With these core features not changing, I opt for you to not buy it. It would be a recommend if there was multiplayer support (not even with pvp elements) to counter the lack of creativity in the single player experience. 

That said, I don't recommend this title unless it's on sale for AT LEAST 50%. I'm already invested, so I might as well play it here and there. Still waiting on maybe one more patch.

No Man's Sky is a game that was tragically overhyped both by its community and its developers. It raised expectiations so high that it could never have fulfilled them all. To many it was a major disappointment, frustratingly grindy and simplistic. It is out of the question that the conduct of the developers was not okay. I assume that in their desire to keep as much of the game wrapped in mystery they ended up promising too much by simply not denying enough. And yes, there were some features promised that were not delivered, for example "meeting other players". 

It is unfortunate that this is what many will remember the game for, because in actuality, it is a very special game - I would even call it a true gem. However, even now that the hype has utterly died, you should really ask yourself wheter or not this game is something that may appeal to you. 

This is still difficult because trying to get reasonably objective reviews is difficult - many let their views of the game be clouded by all the disappointment, while others have still not given up on the fanboi-ism and defend the game and its flaws without critical thought. The thing is - objective reviews won't actually help you that much. Wheter or not you like this game is impossible for anyone but yourself to predict:

Wheter or not this game appeals to you probably won't depend on its graphics or sound or technology or story or gameplay, really.
I think it will appeal to you if you love exploration. 
If you like to take your time,
marvel at the litte differences (because there are not many huge ones), 
if you appreciate the beautiful vista in front of you RIGHT NOW, 
spend a few seconds to think of a cool name for every discovery,
if you see the gameplay as a means to an end - not victory, not progress, but as a means to enable more unique experiences. 

Or, to put it otherwise:
If you are a goal-driven gamer, or someone who values good gameplay, this game - at its core - will probably not be the game for you. If you play it in that way, you will be frustrated by the grind, and if you power through it, it will leave you deeply dissatisfied. You will only see the frustrating search for that one particular thing you need to progress, when really progress is pointless. Nothing ever fundamentally changes. The gameplay progression is entirely superficial, because there really is no progression in this game. Sure, your inventory becomes larger and your shields stronger, but if the point of the game is to get to the end, you dont need any of this. The game doesn't become more challenging and it doesn't reward you for playing well. It is not that type of game.

I think the point of the game is to experience it. And I do really think that a good way is to do it in a zen-like manner: Live in the moment. Appreciate that the things you see no one else has seen, and probably no one else ever will. Treat every discovery as just that, a discovery. If it is another batch of just the thing you can use right now, or something that you never will use doesn't really matter. You will find what you need eventually. There is no point in making a mad dash for it, because in No Man's Sky, truly, the journey is the only real reward.

[h1]What I Think About No Man's Sky (as of the Pathfinder Update)[/h1]

[code]This game (obviously) had a rocky launch riddled with many [i]many[/i] bugs and gameplay issues. If you would've asked me back then what I thought about this game, I would've laughed and said that it was quite frankly a joke. Half the advertised features were either not what they were advertised as or simply nonexistent. The performance on even the best computers could only be described as horrid, and even if you managed to play with the low framerates, you would certainly run into a gamebreaking glitch that forced you to load up an earlier save. However, a lot of that has changed.

HelloGames upheld complete radio silence, leaving many to think that they had simply abandoned the game after getting their money. However, about four months later, they came back with the Foundation Update, "The first of many." The game recieved an entire basebuilding feature as well as new HUD elements, freighters, survival mode, and more. The game recieved much more optimization as well as more bugfixes. While this was a major step in the right direction, the game still had its fair share of bugs and optimization issues. Many gameplay elements were unfair, either being too easy or too hard. HelloGames may have released a good update, but it was still not enough.

After another three months, HelloGames has released another update with more features than the last one. They improved upon the game, both gameplay-wise and graphically. A new vehicle was added, allowing for quicker travel on the planet's surface. Optimization and quality-of-life changes made the game even better and giving it more shape.

While this game certainly still isn't what people were initially expecting, it has already drastically changed since initial release.

As for whether or not I'd buy this game, with only the knowledge of the gameplay mechanics I wouldn't spend a full $60 on this game. However, with the knowledge of how devoted HelloGames is to making this a great game added onto how good of a game it already is, I would most definitely pay full price on this game. Overall, my current score for the game is an 8/10. It's a really good game currently, but it's still not the best game out there.[/code]

So I've spent over 500 hours with No Man's Sky on the PS4 and just recently started playing on PC.  First off, this game is not for everyone.  If you are looking for a story driven game or one with lots of action then this probably isn't the game for you.  One of the reasons that I love NMS is that I love open world/giant sandbox type games.  In the past, I've played such games as Red Dead Redemption, GTA, Fallout 4 and Skyrim. I found myself just wandering around these open worlds and taking everything in, the missions became secondary to exploration. 

No Man's Sky is a very chill, meditative, tranquil experience that is ALL about exploration with some aspects of space combat. The visuals are stunning and the soundtrack is amazing. The game definitely does not hold your hand and while there is no storyline, no missions, no cinematic cutscenes, there is a very in-depth backstory/lore to the game.  This often gets overlooked but if you take the time to read the interactions with the Atlas Interface, Alien Monoliths and Plaques, you can piece together the history of the Alien Races and it's a pretty interesting story.

There is a new Survival Mode which is a very nice addition and at times, feels like it's how the game is meant to be played.  They have also added base building, freighters, side quests and will continue to provide more free content updates which will improve NMS over time.

** Post Path Finder Update **

Just wanted to drop my two cents on the latest free content update.  A bunch of new features have been added including the addition of land vehicles (on home planet), owning multiple starships and storing on your freighter, visiting other players bases, create a race mode (haven't played this yet) and an amazing upgraded photo mode.  And many other in game features.

My recommendation has only been strengthened by the latest update and really looking forward to what they have in store for the next one.

PATH FINDER UPDATE REVIEW:

I got back to this game again after a while. The base building from the Foundation update were really time consuming and never really interests me much. And now, they come with Path Finder update which really excited me very much. You all know about the Exocrafts' buggy/rover, so I will not talk much about them.

The devs really listens and they addresses our complaints, even currently not all the issues were addressed. I really appreciated that.

Now the ship type matters; do you want to do (uninspiring) dogfights? get fighter ship. Do you want to store as many resources you can get? Get a cargo ship. But I don't see how this will works with the existing players with existing 48 slots ship. Aside from ship type, they also now come with classes. My current ship is C rank, which means I will need to embark a journey to get a better rank ship for better stats.

Multitools also get the same treatment with the ship. It comes in different types and classes, each one good for at least one specific purpose. Mine was C-rank Rifle. Again, I'm now have a personal objective to get a better multitool.

Also, did I mention that they are now come with stats? You will know how much damage your ship can handle before it blows, how much damage you can deal with your weapon.. and there's damage number which will pop if you hit enemy ships/creatures/minerals, which made this game more RPG-ish. Of course, you can disable this from the menu.

The Devs gave me purpose to play this game again; to get the best ship + multitools + home planet + great exocraft. But I'm still disappointed with the exocraft that only works on the home planet. I hope we can teleport them to any planet via buildable station. I'm sure this will be addressed in the future.. (for we already can teleport ship back and forth home base to/from space station).

Kudos to the dev team, I hope you can deliver more exciting updates in the next upcoming three or four months.

And if possible, please make no man's sky be able to run in older machines. It doesn't need to be very good in graphical terms.. at least, make them playable.

The next most boring fun game in the universe is all about going planetside, something us Eve Online players have always wanted to be able to do. Must have for Eve players. Very relaxing, somewhat tedious play that helps calm the nerves.

-Post 1.2 Review

Pro's
I'm loving the new Pathfinder update. 
-Although I have yet to make one in survival, the new ground vehicles are a blast.
-Finally, the factions are starting to come into play a bit, with the purchase of blueprints based on your standing with each faction. 
-Not all rocks and plants give common elements now. And a new currency for blue prints.
-Class system for star ships and multi-tool (Fighters, Exploration... etc...) with different specializations. (I was waiting for this feature since day 1 and was very disappointed when it wasn't in game on release.)
-Grade system for star ships and multi tool which affect base stats of each.
-Looks like there is a bit more diversity to the fauna on each planet. (I hope they keep adding more)


Con's
-Still a lot of optimization needs to be done graphically. Maybe it's just me, but I get some flashing textures on grassy planets.
-Ground vehicles are a bit buggy.
-No real interaction between factions as of yet. I would like to see more space battles and rivalries between them. (Maybe struggle for control over different systems.)
-No multiplayer (yes I know this one's kind of beating a dead horse. See more opinions below on a personal opinion of how to deal with multiplayer.) By the way I'm not saying all or even most aspects of the game should be.

More Opinions
-Still lacking content. I know the overall intent of the game is to go to the center of the galaxy, but it's in need of substance. And by substance I mean things to do along the way. (Boss battles or giant creatures maybe? Abandoned space stations and Explorable Ruins? Just saying...)
-Multiplayer instancing. Maybe make select elements of the game, like the one's stated above in my still lacking content opinion, multiplayer. Having a crew of 6-8 friends and random people instanced in an Abandoned Space Station or Faction space battle sounds kind of interesting to me.

Should you buy it? Again this game is still not for everyone. If you are looking for multiplayer first person shooter with straight action 90% of the time, this game is not for you. If you like exploring and about 60% action (depends on what mode you play) with with some elements of base building and customization, maybe this game is for you. No Man's Sky has come a long way from it's initial release and it still has a long way to go. With the way their updates have been rolling out, I'm really hopeful of what the final product will look like.

Having delved into the modding scene, waited around for patches, and given this game a lengthy break between my initial review upon release and now... I think I can honestly say i'm happy with my purchase finally.

It is by no means a perfect game. It was incredibly overhyped, missing features we were promised (and still is, in a few cases), it ran pretty poorly, and it was overall just an incredibly bland, boring experience with not a whole lot worth checking out. It was, honestly, an Early Access title branded as a full fledged complete $60 game.

Now, though? It's better. It's still not perfect, and it is still very much flawed. But it's enjoyable. Between the various updates Hello Games has released, and a very active modding community, a good amount of stuff has been added and a number of things that weren't present in the final version compared to the E3 demos are back in some form. You can now see massive trees, giant dinosaurs, and all manner of incredible landscapes with the help of a few mods thanks to the game's community. There's a creative mode  for just faffing about (Although, annoyingly, you still have to get the hyperdrive upgrades to find the really cool worlds, which seems like something you should have from the start in Creative, of all things). You can build bases, explore rough terrain quickly with rovers and exocraft, and hire freighters for storing all your junk.

It's better. It really is. It's still not quite what we were promised, and it still has a lot of work that needs to be done, but i'm finding myself enjoying it, and looking forward to firing it up so I can chill out and explore space. It's... honestly fun.

I'd give this game 6/10, but I'm going to award it a bonus point for encouraging me to re-download Spore and to start playing that instead.

Spore.........what No Mans Sky should have been!

UPDATE (16th April 17) 

So after a few months away from this game after an initial 40 hours of play, I decided to revisit it given the addition of some new updates. 

I have to say, I've actually been pretty damn impressed with the amount of improvements the developers have added, and the fact they've actually listened and reacted to the community (for example, hearing people's frustrated feedback about only being able to use vehicles on home planets, they updated it to include all planets instead). 

I hadn't actually followed this game much prior to it's launch last year, and I think that not having any expectations like that meant I wasn't left as disappointed or annoyed as a lot of folks out there were. That said, the game did get kinda boring quite quickly (after my initial OCD like tendencies to mine and order everything died off haha). 

I'm still currently finding my feet again in this game after having picked up where I left off, but so far what I'm most impressed by is: 

The new base building system - this adds mini quests, farming, and a chance to personalize something you can take a bit of pride in, (not to mention the addition of storage units for your materials!!)

The new planetary exploration vehicles - there are 3 types of new mobile mining/combat units, from small and agile to large and bulky, and they make both resource gathering and exploring planets more fun and less 'grindy'. 

The addition of new resources all together, special resources that require equipment to obtain them, and I LOVE how when you now scan a planet, you see the TYPE of each resource rather than just the colour (e.g TH for thamium, PT for platinum, ZN for Zinc etc). 

You can now buy, staff and grow crops on these HUGE freighter ships. I've only come across one so far and it costs around 67 million to buy, so that'll keep me busy for a while), but how awesome! 

I could go on, but to conclude I really do encourage those who bought this game and dropped it, to pick it back up again and see what you think. I'm sure you'll agree that whilst far from perfect, it's certainly heading in the right direction and the developers are starting to pull a few rabbits out of the hat now. 

Review therefore changes to recommended, and my score now goes to 7/10, without the need for me to play Spore instead :-). 

Well done devs, maybe you'll creep back on to my 2017 Christmas card list yet!!

Hi! This is an update to my previous review(back in August 2016).

So there has obviously been a few super awesome updates to the game, and they have done nothing but make the game even better than what it previously had been(still super pissed about no multiplayer but whatever)!

1. Survival;  This aspect of the game has been severely improved since its initial release in August. 

A. The ore collection has only improved, what with the implementation of the advanced laser beam and the Hazmat Glove, including the introduction of several new ore types and forms of collection(mining from space still needs to be HEAVILY improved[but this is just my opinion]). 

B. With the addition of base building it allows us players to actually settle a primary home/base of operations to better organize our exploratory expenditures into the unknown depths of space. They also provide assistance in the cultivation of the more 'rare' elements that we have almost no way of acquiring except for feeding animals and praying to whatever creator you believe in(don't care what you believe in it makes no difference to me) that you MIGHT get the element. Base building also allows us to express ourselves and our own sense of self by designing and building amazing(or not so amazing) bases that we call home. <3

C. Combat is still pretty much point and shoot, although the recent update(Per 3/17/2017-ISH date/time) there have been a few new forms of firing options, such as a kind of gatling upgrade, and also this railgun-like charge(called a vulcan???) and the grenade launcher has been revamped slightly to do more damage. (I really don't have much to say about combat, enemies and largely lacking, although not without good reason, this game IS based on EXPLORATION, not Combat.)

D. Exocrafts!! That simple little word conveys(IMO) the best addition to the game so far! Wether its the fast AF little Nomad with its hover pads <3 or the mid-range Roamer capable of moving quickly across the terrain and destroying things by simply ramming into them(and also providing decent inventory storage), or maybe your someone like me who prefers a massive inventory storage then its the Colossus for us! Each has its own particulars, an example is the Nomad is light armoured but fast AF and the Colossus is slow AF but heavily armoured. Each has benefits and hinderances but you'll find your fit. :3

E, ALMOST FORGOT!! You can buy super huge freighters to storage up to a maximum of 5 ships(because they added ship/weapon classes) and you can also have the freighter warp to whatever system your in allowing you to have a mobile farming base and save location and whatnot, improving your survivability Ten-Fold(if your in Survival mode[in 'Classic' it improves One-Hundred Fold] ) 

2. Gamemodes;

A. Yeah this are kinda self explanatory, but here we go! The first mode is the Original 'Classic' mode which has a relaxed(though not peacful) experience where you roam through the galaxy pretty much following(or not) the basic 'plot' or the game.

B. Survival is basically 'Classic' on crack. Pretty funny statement huh? Well its true, Survival is VERY DIFFICULT in that most planets are hard AF to survive on and resources are generated and given maybe 35-50% less than the regular mode. So good luck with that mode you gentle explorers!

C. Permadeath is obviously the worst, because it combines Survival mode with the fact that you get ONE LIFE ONLY and everything gets wiped if you die. So its pretty freaking bad.

D. Creative... I'm sorry but i have never used this mode and i never will to be honest, so i can't give an accurate description of it. I just think(IMO) that it is sacrilegious to not play this game with some for of 'death' included, since death is CERTAINLY a part of the game.

TL;DR
So to recap, this game has good Mining/Resource collection, but bad combat(cause its not a combat PRIMARY game).
It has awesome base building where you can expand and explore to your hearts content! There are massive Freighters that act as mobile bases(if you can pile together a couple Million Credits to buy one).  There are awesome new Exocraft vehicles to use to drive around and whatnot. And there are a variety of different gamemodes that interest whichever type of playstyle you happen to prefer.

This is a tough review to write. I followed this game closely for a year and a half or so. I was incredibly excited for it and really wanted to like it. If you look at my play time, you'll see that I played it for quite a while, and I even enjoyed quite a bit of that time.

So why the thumbs down? There is a lack of content and the game isn't worth $60. If this was a $20 or $30 early access title, it'd be a lot easier to like. Hello Games has been releasing quite a few updates, mostly focused on fixing crashes and game bugs, but they have said they plan to release extra content down the line (specifically base building and owning freighters). Will these features add to the game? Maybe a bit, but I don't imagine they'll change my overall opinion. Mods also improve the experience quite a bit, but it doesn't seem like the developers should get the benefit of the doubt for the community's efforts in modding the game.

Pros:
- They did hit that 70s sci-fi aesthetic.
- Exploring your first few planets is fun and interesting.
- The music and sound design is great.
- You can hop in your ship, fly out into space, and then fly to a planet and land.
- There are a few interesting things to see, and there are some real screenshot worthy moments.

Cons:
- There are only maybe 6 types of planet biomes. There's really not a ton of variation within this.
- There are only a couple dozen types of different creatures. Sure, you might see one with horns or one that's bigger, but you start to see a lot of the same types of things repeatedly.
- There are only a few types of space stations and the general interior layout is the same.
- Inventory management is a headache.
- Survival aspects get in the way of exploring. Should have focused more on diversity of content and generation and less on micromanagement gameplay.
- There are major graphical issues. Pop-in is unpleasant and textures are ugly.
- A lot of things that were shown in the lead-in to launch aren't in the game. You can't see other players, the graphics aren't as good, flora and fauna are smaller than in the trailers, and several other things.
- The factions are kind of pointless. The three alien races are pretty much the same as far as how you interact with them. Just a different skin.

I could probably list some more stuff, but the bottom line is that this is a fun experience for let's say 5 to 10 hours, but it needs some serious updates or redesigns to make it a game you'll want to play for long times and feel happy about. Maybe worth checking out when it's on sale or after several updates have added to it.

Traditional Score: 6/10 (Where's a sideways thumb when you need one?)

Foundation version 1.1 update:

Okay. This update helped a lot. They implemented base building in a way that encourages exploration. There have been a lot of small changes that are positive from making minerals and building more spread out to improving the UI and accessibility. The graphics are improved as well and space combat is quite a bit better. Creatures can get a bit bigger than before and planets can have more variety and be more interesting. I'm not ready to label the game a resounding success or anything just yet, but a couple more updates like this and it could be something special.

Pathfinder 1.2 Update:

Now we're talking. Graphical improvements, quality of life improvements, and planetary vehicles implemented in a way that there's a point to using them. At this point, I think this is a unique and interesting game worth checking out if it appeals to you. There actually is a "game" now instead of completely open ended wandering. I'm changing my review to a thumbs up.

EDIT: 3/15/17 PathFinder update

Grudgingly, I am giving No Man's Sky a thumbs up now--with one caveat. This is still not a 60 dollar a game. Wait for a Steam sale when it is 50% off--or more.

The Foundation and Pathfinder updates move NMS into what I would call a playable, and at many times, fun, game. There is now a gameplay loop and there is actually a rarity to certain items that was not there before. With the rovers, freighters and base building, they are getting closer to a complete game.

Terrain generation on planets is much, much improved. I have seen some truly interesting features that were not there in 1.0. I also am more impressed with the distribution of points of interests on planet surfaces. Gone are the days of finding a new POI every 2 minutes away in every direction. Some planets have lots, many have a few and some have barely any. There is a progression system now in ships and multi-tools as well.

The game still needs more--there needs to be a reason to go in caves, animals need a wider array of behavior patterns and movements and there needs to be more to fight than just sentinel drones when on planet surfaces. There also needs to be more procedural generated creation variety. I'm still seeing alot of the same thing scattered across various planets. There is still no story to speak of, and no ending either.

In conclusion, if its on sale, No Man's Sky is now, almost 7 months later, a worthwhile purchase.

***********End Edit

Not much more to say beyond what has already been said. In 30 years of gaming, I have never seen a game launch in such an incomplete mess as No Man's Sky. There is no 'game' here. I am going to hold out hope that HG and modders can make this into something worthwhile by 4Q 2016 or 1Q 2017, but at this point there is nothing to really do other than take screenshots of the planets you land on. The lack of features is staggering.

Pros:

-Amazing alien landscapes
-Beautiful color palette
-Impressive music

Cons

-Planets are all the same aside from a different paint job.
-There appears to be no understanding or recognition of how to actually put a progression system into the game. Most resources are available on all planets. You are always within 2 minutes on foot travel time to a point of interest that will be repeated over and over again across the planet and every other planet. Caves usually do not have any reason to explore them. Oceans do not have any reason to explore them. Planets do not, ultimately, have any reason to explore them.
-Inventory management is a nightmare in the early game.
-There is shallow progression in ship, multi-tool and exosuit upgrades.
-Shallow story.
-Game endings are non-existent to outright insulting.
-There is very little to do other than sight-see and upgrade. After you have your upgrades, only sight-seeing.

This game may really be interesting in 6 months to a year. Or not.

I've only put about 5 hours into the game since it came out on PC, and I guess I have a few things I could say:

1-The game, at its core, is about exploration, and it accomplishes that. There is DEFINITELY plenty to explore, but unlike other open-world games, you cannot explore all of it, which the completionist in me dislikes a little. But it is supposed to be that way.

2-The game plays pretty smoothe for the most part, so long as you have the specs for it and change some of the default settings.

3-That said, some of the defaults are questionable, such as a default cap of 30fps for example. And the fact you have to restart the game in order to actually change these settings.

4-The content is sparse. Although it is procedurally generated, a lot of the planets feel and look the same, as well as the creatrures and environments. The first thirty minutes consist of gathering, walking and flying, and this continues throughout the game without much variance.

5-If this is a game about farming resources, which it shouldn't be, then the inventory should be much larger than it is. I fill up my inventory so fast that I'm dropping items every twenty seconds.

6-The gameplay is okay, but that's about it. Combat isn't very fun, and it's mostly confusing why enemies attack. The rest is just walking around or flying around slowly to get from place to place to find the same stuff you already have.

So there are a few things that can be better, such as base building, colonization, online multiplayer, larger inventory, etc. It is by no means the worst game of all time, nor is it bad. It's just not that great, or not as great as we were told it was going to be. It feels more like space-minecraft without the craft. It's mediocre at best, but this is an indie-game, so the expectations shouldn't be that high. With all that said, I would maybe recommend this to someone if Hello-Games added new, FREE content to the game (since it's 60$ already) and if this someone liked pure exploration and discovery.

I hope this review was helpful to anyone thinking about buying or refunding it!

EDIT: It is nice to see that they are updating the game with new content that people are wanting, such as said base-building. Hopefully this game continues to grow and regain respect from its players. However, I still stand by my previous statements and do not reccomend purchasing it. At least not yet. And for those of us who have pucrchased it, at least there is SOME new stuff.

Well, I feel I should've seen this one coming.

Yes, I was looking forward to the game, but I wasn't hyped the same way many others were. From the start, I figured this would be a niche game that only appeals to a certain audience. In a way, my prediction was right. But at the same time, I feel like this game could've been so much better.

Now don't get me wrong, I give this game a thumbs down but by no means do I "not recommend" this game. There is the possibility that you will absolutely adore No Man's Sky. I give it a negative review because I would prefer you wait until the performance issues are fixed and the price drops.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]

I really wish I could say something good about the graphics here, but I really can't. It seems pretty at first glance, but once you look into it you begin to see how low-quality the textures are. Not to mention the novelty of the colorful planets wear off incredibly fast. It seems nice, but as time goes on, you begin to see that the graphics are still dull, no matter how much color there is. The idea of the visuals here was to place you in a poster for a 70's sci fi film, and I didn't feel that way for a single moment during my time with this game.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

The gameplay has the same issue. At first, you'll be awestruck, because from a technological standpoint, it's hard not to be impressed by the size of the game. But you know the phrase, "quantity isn't quality"? Well, it applies here. This game is huge, and I'm glad that it's this way, but what it has in size it lacks in depth. Every planet has different creatures and can vary in appearance, but once you get over that you realize that there isn't much variation with the planets, and everything feels the same. I do like the idea of having the survival aspect to the game, but it doesn't feel right because No Man's Sky is so easy. If you're running low on something, let's say that your life support systems are pretty low. All you need to do is walk a few feet and get some carbon, and BOOM, you're as good as new. You do stuff like this all throughout the game, and when you pair that with the repetitive exploration, you'll realize that this game is incredibly boring after a short period of time. Oh, and the combat? Clunky. Killing Sentinels is such a drag, and I find the space battles tedious more than anything. This game focused too much on exploration, and neglected other elements that would've made this game so much better.

[h1]Story[/h1]

No story, there is a small amount of lore but the rest is up to you. This won't be counted towards the final score.

[h1]Audio[/h1]

This is one of the only things that makes No Man's Sky any good. The sound effects and all of that aren't anything to write home about, what IS good however is the music. I'll say whatever I want to say about this game, but I won't argue about the "soundtrack". While the rest of the game is [i]eh[/i], the music is very fitting and I love taking a breather to listen to it. This game's music is one of the only redeeming factors for it.

[h1]Replayability[/h1]

In the case of No Man's Sky, I feel you'll get less playtime out of it than you'd think. You might commit and beat the game, but [spoiler]all that happens is that you start the game over on New Game+ or whatever you'd call it.[/spoiler] By then, you'll be groaning and you'll give up on the game.

[h1]Verdict[/h1]

No Man's Sky isn't terrible, it's just painfully mediocre. There are some ideas I like, but they didn't quite work. The one thing to this game I absolutely loved was the music, and even then it's not one of those games that you'd buy for the soundtrack alone. There are some aspects to the game that aren't terrible, but I feel their potential wasn't maximized here. If I were you, I would hold off on buying the game, but I won't stop you if you really believe you'll enjoy it. My reviews should not be the final decision, after all. The choice is entirely yours.

TL;DR It's a good game, but for people who like exploration and have a good computer.

Pros: A vast universe to be explored, beautiful cenario, many upgrades to unlock at your ship, multitool and exosuit.

Cons: Require a fairly good computer to run it smooth, not a game for people uninterested in exploration, don't have a story or objectives out of explorate, lack of promissed multiplayer.

Price: A bit expensive considering all but hard to say not worth for the target public. On eventual 25/50% may be worth even for people just looking for wasting a few hours wandering around and enjoying some uncompromised play.

------------

First of all, keep in mind that this game require a fairly good PC to run smoth, by myself I've been playing for days had not any major issues, some friends with older but still strong computers had some or need to restart the game every few hours to keep it smoth.
Those exploration open world (galaxy?) games have a story of requering a good PC to run them so nothing surprising here when we consider the size of the game world/universe.

I would be lying to say I'm not loving that game, but would be lying too if said I had not been disapointed about some aspects, mainly the so promissed multiplayer ("players will be able to meet each other") that aways been so vague about, but while pretty hard to aways was said that we WOULD be able to meet other players. (The game was aways listes as SinglePlayer on Steam, so a bit fool of us for believing so, but promisses were made anyway.)

Still for anyone who enjoy exploration it's a amazing game! To run by your heart desire at numberless planets, upgrading your gear and ship and seeing beautiful cenarios, it's a dream for most players who like this genre.
I see a ton of negative reviews and most seen to be about the lack of the promissed multiplayer, computers not being able to run it smoth or at all, and people who were hoping for something else than a exploration game.

Hello Games had their fair share of blame for letting the game hype getting too bit, making vague promisses and never denying what people would hope or guess about, and anyway selling it at a AAA game price, but the game is still a pretty enjoyable experience.

My 3rd edit and hopefully last one:

Who i recommend this game to: If you want to chill out, listen to awesome soundtracks, look at beautiful procedural terrain, laught at weird animals, and just generraly, have fun, then this is the game for you. If you look for a hardcore survival game that will make you pull your hair out, maybe this is the game for you as well. Don't look for a deep, undermining story, or non stop space action, because this is not about that, the normal, survival and hardcore difficulties are very grindy. Sure there are space fight, but you will spend most your time on the planets, gathering resources.
Look up youtube videos, search the reddit for screenshots, decide for yourself if you like the game or not.

To those who already refunded, or will never play the game again: I don't blame you at all, we were fucked over, but the devs made up for it. I am dissapointed in myself about trying to refund the game twice. I knew they were working on an update, but was angry at them for lying, and not telling us anything. But that is for a different rant...

Now regarding both the 1.1 and 1.2 updates. 

First let's talk about 1.1:
 It was THE update we were waiting for. It brought so much new stuff into the game that it was finally safe to say "it's worth the money". The whole new terrain generation, the new plants, basebuilding, they all added to making NMS into a completely different game.
The grind is still tedious and boring, but at least now we have a reason to go out and explore the new planets. 
1.2: Haven't really fiddled around with it that much, (4.4 hours as of now). Got all the new vehicles and am working on getting every new stuff. 
The steam workshop integration is probably my favourite of the bunch. It gives players the option to share the base they built, be it a small starter base, up to giant 6 star motels in the most beutiful places. 
The vehicles are fun. The roamer feels like the Meko from Mass Effect 1... (ptsd anyone?)

It's clear that the launch was a wake up call for the devs. They realized that people are passionate about this game and that we were very, very dissapointed. They shut themselves in to make 1.1 (which was not how they should've handled it), and are now delivering on everything they promissed, and more. Actual multiplayer next? I can hope right....

I once again change my review from negative back to recommended. The reason beeing: It's fun to play again.

If you are planning to buy the game, and you can't wait for a sale, it's now worth the full price, but i'd still recommend waiting for a sale. 
"and i am waiting 2-3 years till it gets actually better." i said in my last review. I can safely say that in that time the game will be something people remember not for it's failure at the start, but as an artistic masterpiece. Why? Because of the modding community, and the people who are keeping the game alive. Reddit is filled with beautiful screenshots, people modding their game to have even more stuff, and a Galactic Hub Project. 

TL;DR: the game is worth the price, and is good

Reviews.205070:
[b][u]See written review below[/u][/b], or watch it here: https://youtu.be/YSCb8r2xEY8
[h1]THIS IS A MIXED REVIEW!! TL;DR: SKIP TO CONCLUSION![/h1]

No Man’s Sky is a procedurally generated first person sci-fi game that is almost entirely focused on exploration and discovery.

You fly around in your ship, exploring planets, and the vastness of space. Land on the planets to discover new technologies, meet new aliens, learn their languages, and analyze and catalog a wide variety of plants and animals across the universe. The amount of content to explore is completely mindblowing, and if you love exploring just for the sake of it, there is a lot to do. However, there is also a lot of repetition, and potential monotony that will likely turn a lot of people off of the game.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[list][*]excellent exploration game with tons of planets for those who simply love to explore without needing a reason to, or those who enjoy collecting everything
[*]survival aspects are usually fairly easy to manage, and don't feel like a burden; on some planets with extreme conditions, upgrades to your suit are extremely beneficial
[*]a good amount of technology upgrades for your tool, ship, and suit to discover
[*]decent crafting system because it’s easy to follow, and very clear about what materials are still needed
[*]ground combat is alright; it isn’t difficult, and it can keep you on your toes on some planets
[*]the game looks beautiful; it’s absolutely gorgeous with the many vibrant colours on the environments both on land and in space - many of the visuals feel fresh and exciting
[*]there’s a wide variety of ship designs and colours, and it’s great that you can buy any ship that you encounter if you can afford it
[*]many of the creature designs are unique, and some are very strange looking
[*]the audio is decent; the music and ambience are enjoyable
[*]the voice dialog in the alien languages is a neat feature, and it’s interesting that you can learn words to understand different alien languages[/list]

[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[list][*]doesn’t seem to have a persistent story, or any missions to give the player objectives - I’m trying to get to the centre of the universe, but I don’t really know why (I generally enjoy exploration, but I need to have purpose, or incentive to explore)
[*]for those who get tired of exploring, and want to get to the centre, progress feels much too slow and underwhelming
[*]could use better tutorials because there isn’t much that explains how things work, or what you should do, and you have to figure things out as you go
[*]no option to start a new game
[*]major lack of save slots (there are only two slots for your most recent auto-saves); the option to manually save would be a great addition as well
[*]technology upgrades take up inventory space, and items that are not resources don’t stack
[*]after a while of playing, most of the technology items found are duplicates of things already known, and it’s very discouraging to be rewarded with basically nothing after searching many new locations; duplicate technology should be removed, or at least give a decent amount of currency reward instead
[*]crafting certain items can become very tedious, and inconvenient (for example: to make one warp fuel, you have to craft each of the previous items individually before making the final product even if you have all the mats)
[*]there is no way to buy the technology patterns you actually want, and you need to be lucky to get it by random chance discovery (I’m mainly referring to the warp drive technology upgrades because you need specific types of warp drive upgrades in order to jump to certain types of solar systems that are supposedly more rich in resources)
[*]air combat is very annoying especially close to the planet surface; it feels awkward trying to dogfight, and the ship movement and controls feel sluggish (dogfighting in Planetside 2 is much, much more fun than the air combat in No Man’s Sky)
[*]bug where three separate anomalies that were supposed to be black holes, but they never showed up on my galactic map at all
[*]galactic map is a nuisance to use: selecting the jump route is a huge pain, and the map view changes on you every time you look at a new location, so it’s easy to get disoriented (I wish there was a way to just jump max distance possible more easily)
[*]some assets that heavily overused: the space stations are all practically identical on the inside, most of the enemies you encounter are the same, many of the plants and resource structures are the same from one planet to the next, and building designs are repetitive, and it’s not very satisfying to discover the exact same buildings over and over on every single planet 
[*]I didn’t experience any graphical bugs, but I did encounter some periodic frame drops, a few crashes to desktop, and a couple other times where I started lagging so badly that I had to restart the game for it to be playable again
[*]some other annoyances that the game has: 1. when you save at an outpost, there is basically the same animation every single time, 2. when you encounter aliens (without even talking to them yet) the change to letterbox is completely unnecessary, 3. targeting reticule is small and sometimes hard to see, so I often was using the building directional icon as my reticule by mistake when trying to target things (I'd like to see the building icons moved further away from the reticule, or other reticule options), and 4. the most annoying of all is when the journey milestone achievements popup, you have to wait for all the spammy popups to go away before you can start playing again[/list]

[h1]Conclusion:[/h1]
No Man’s Sky is most certainly a game about the journey and not the end. It is not a game that will appeal to everyone. I enjoyed the game for about 10 hours or so, and after that I decided to head towards the centre. In total, I wound up playing for over 27 hours, but the last 12 hours felt so painful, and incredibly tedious. Progress to the centre feels too slow and underwhelming, and I am not even close to getting there. The game has a lot of content, but lacks purpose, and gets repetitive. For people who enjoy collectibles, and exploring just for the sake of exploring, they’ll likely get a lot of enjoyment out of the game, even at full price. On the other hand, if you aren’t keen on exploring endlessly, then this is probably not the game for you, especially at its hefty price tag. No Man’s Sky has a ton of potential, but there is definitely room for improvement.

Update:

TL;DR: If you're checking this out for the first time, ignore the baggage of older reviews disappointed in the initial release, 2017 NMS is a great game! If you're a day one buyer, check out the new patches, I think you'll be pleased.

Bought this game day one, played for a while hoping it'd be good and gave up, hadn't played in months. Yesterday I installed the Pathfinder update and played about 6 hours straight without leaving my first system. Previously the game was mediocre at best, the core mechanic/promise of being able to go from planet to space seamlessly was neat but there was basically nothing else to the game.

Base building, land vehicles, ships, weapons etc introduced with the last two patches have made this a completely different game. While I'm still not pleased about the shenanigans surrounding the initial game release, I can pretty easily recommend this to a new player.

If you've been on the fence about this game or have just found it now, don't hesitate to pick it up. The initial negative reviewers were justifiably angry about Hello Games' marketing vs the actual game (generously described as "underdelivering", less generously described as "outright lies"). Don't let the baggage from the initial release rob you of a game that's actually pretty good now.

If you're a day one buyer like me, who was pretty disillusioned by the initial release, it's worth taking a look at now. The game is much closer to the original promise (the rational, non-hyped promise) of freedom to explore or build a new life. 

I'm cautiously optimistic that future patches will improve the game further, and while I'm not pleased with how we got here (the terrible initial release, the months of silence, etc), I am quite satisfied today.

6/10

Reviews.206011:
[TLDR: Came back from the brink.]

Back in 2016, I had wrote a review on No Man's Sky when it had first launched. My opinion was rather negative, which comes to no surprise considering how polarizing it was in its initial state. While Hello Games had laid down the foundation (har, har) of the game, they built nothing else upon it, delivering unto us an incredibly tedious and bare-bones survival sandbox with little to no point to playing it.

Now it's 2017. Formerly, the idea of Hello Games continuing to support what many considered to be a dead game was nothing more than wishful thinking, but with the delivery of the Foundation and Path Finder updates (which are completely free overhauls), it goes to show just how much the studio is willing to appease their understandably angry playerbase. Base building, land-based vehicular exploration, and Steam Workshop integration with a plethora of fixes and features shape the game to resemble more of what we expected from the game at launch. While I still do not agree with a $60 price tag, it's definitely worth a buy if you happen to catch it being on sale.

[PROS:]
+Eye-catching art style reminiscent of old sci-fi novel covers.
+Continued support from Hello Games to improve the game.
+Steam Workshop integration to finally get those online features in-game.
+Great modding community with their own fixes and improvements to the game.
+Way too many planets to explore.
+You finally get to name your own weapons and ships (I'm calling mine the Normandy).
+Land-based vehicular hijinks.
+Versatile base-building system to grab your own slice of space heaven.
+Spaceship controls are still satisfying and easy to handle, especially in space combat.
+When you actually run engage in combat, it's satisfying to gun down robots and towering creatures.
+A plethora of different difficulties and modes to suit your needs (I recommend Survival to spice the game up a bit).
+Explore bases built by other players, giving more reason to check out more planets.
+An actual mission log!

[CONS:]
-The "ending" to the game when you reach the core is still shite.
-A few optimization issues on PC, but nothing completely deal-breaking.

First and foremost to those of you with a Nvidia card, like myself, be sure to play this thing in borderless window mode and turn vsync off. If you have a GSync monitor then you are good to go. I have been getting about 132 FPS average with the following:

I7 6700k OC 7% to match my RAM

I read the reviews here and I read the developers responses via twitter. I followed the trail of crumbs to common problems  that all pointed to out of date drivers, VC++ 2010 redistritro, and a few mods to the settings file. Easy enough I thought and took the leap. What I found was a game that WITHOUT the corrections runs like a snail up a wall! After the changes I could not ask for better considering what this game is and what it does seamlessly. So the bugs? I have 16.6 hours thus far put into it and I have not had a crash, but after 5 hours it does slow and needs a restart. So there is a cache problem in there somewhere....oh well, takes 30 seconds and I probably should not be playing that long anyway BUT this game is awesome!

So there was a game a long time ago called Star Control II. This is Star Control II in first person. Seriously it is a mirror image of that game. Land on a planet get some resources, meet some aliens, fly to a space station and trade, avoid pirates or kill them. Rinse and repeat! What makes it really cool is the generation of everything in front of you. I have not seen the same thing twice, although the animals (aliens for sure) all kinda follow an odd art design that makes them look like something from Spore. But I love the colors (this game uses colors like Fallout uses brown), and I love the chilled out atmosphere. I play while listening to some oldies and chilled out rock music on iTunes and just let let hours slip by. 

So the big question is it 60 bucks good? If you love the idea of having Star Control again then yes. Yes indeed. If you have no idea check this out, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Control_II, still not sure?, buy Star Control II on GOG and give it about an hour. If you love management of space ship space, trading, intergalactic travel and finding resources in that game then buy NMS. If you want COD in space, buy Destiny and avoid NMS because this is not a combat game.

Low points of the game....
The space ship constantly zeroing itself. Seriously its annoying. 
I do not like not being able to crash into a planet. The devs need to get Descent and play that for the space ship travel.
The ship in space is very very loose, Wing Commander Privateer did the space pirate battles better.

All of that said NMS for me is a really good game. I think I would toss a 8.5 at it if I worked for one of the big review sites. Cool game! Thanks Hello Games, I am going back to grab a warp cell and see if I can make some Sentinals explode!

One last thing, it is okay to hate the game and dispute the release of this thing. It is even okay to express frustration that this thing is not COD in space. It is not okay to complain to an games company when you the computer owner do not meet requirements. Each time this game launches it uploads things to a server and I am positive part of that is your system specs, not that uncommon especially for internet traffic. Yes all your favorite sites do it! When Hello Games says something like 70+ percent of people launching do not have updated drivers or requirements installed I think its time for people to shush and do their part. Just my 2 cents, so update, correct a small line in a file, get some new technology and enjoy!

EDIT 6/12/2017

I returned to the game this past weekend to see if the updates added content and I have to say for a company people accuse of not caring....they sure seem to care. A small dev company releasing free updates of such scale is pretty nice to see. I was flying around and thinking "Huh this seems pretty neat" and BAM hit by bounties, then I found a base, then I managed to roam and found things on the planets I never saw before. Giant monsters and vicious sentinels. Basically Hello Games decided to turn this sucker into Minecraft with limited multiplayer. Would it be better with full multiplayer? You betcha! Will it be added? Who knows, due to the horrible response of the game the company is basicrehoally a dark black hole in the center of the galaxy. Until that comes out you can enjoy the following, bounties, full trading, space combat (rescaled to basically Wing Commander II), escort missions, a full charma system, and basically Minecraft with better graphics. Is it empty? Sort of. Are the worlds similar? Kinda. 

For those who do not understand how something like this works it is pretty simple in concept but very very hard to execute. First you need a few databases of conditions and then an engine to piece it all together on the fly and eventually you get to a machine driven code based game that can generate its own enviornments. Of course that also means you are limited to the constant databases you encoded as the index. Makes sense. 

My wish list varies from others, I would like to see responses to weather. I would love to see fire, ice, actual wind that tosses you about and acid rain that damages your ship. Zelda did this well on Switch and I understand this is a fixed world but the elements are so neat when brought to life. Next on the wish list, Aliens! I want something more that is based on gravity and conditions. Fire planet close to a sun? The animals if any would be particle based or small in nature that has fire scales or rock bodies. Sulfate based lifeforms on Earth show this so lets have some of that! Ice worlds vast with beasts of hair and 27 legs that move so slowly it is annoying. It would be neat to see. Personally I want to build a ship. I do not want to buy it, I do not want to find it, I want to build it! Trade routes and empire growth. I want to be the overlord of these species they have. A trillionare by owning all the ships and judging the dangers of sending them out and about would be pretty cool. Maybe from that factions grow with trade that make friendships that much more valuable. Thats about it. 

I do not care about seeing anyone, playing with anyone, or even if I get to hear anyone. Wing Commander did single player so well I never thought I wanted a pal to hunt with. 

With that I may be the only one out there but thank you Sean. Your vision is a delight to me and honestly I do not regret the 60 bucks day one purchase, nor do I scorn you on the hype. I understand Beta builds and Alpha builds. I also understand selling on a PS4 which is not a PC and what hardware limitations means. 

The problems are a thing of the past and I really look forward to bright future and I will be buying any other Hello Games products you all put out because honestly after a year you all have earned respect from me for supporting this thing, not because you had to, but because you wanted to. You have listened to people hate you for producing a product, the same people complain about EA and call them the worst company ever...First World Problems. The worst company is fair from EA or Hello Games, maybe research Monsanto, KBR, heck take a look at P&G. But I digress, bottom line in this review should be this....

Buy the game and explore. Survive. Have fun! Still a 8.5 and thats pretty awesome!

A wonderland of barren planets (with the occasional lively ones), atmospheric music, custom bases, and starships.

If you need a game that's relaxing, No Man's Sky is for you. If you need a game that makes you feel small and filled with wonder, No Man's Sky is for you. If you like science fictiony worlds, No Man's Sky is for you.

At first the game was TOO chill, with no real goals to keep one occupied. With added base building and missions tied to that, now there are plenty of excuses to explore planets and collect resources to deck out your home. The survival aspect is now well balanced, letting players explore while occasionally asking them to wander a planets surface to keep life support running.

Don't expect to binge play past 2 hours, the game doesn't try to be addicting, it tries to chillinate your mind until you find yourself ready to go to bed/get to work/etc..

BEFORE YOU BUY
If your looking for an action game filled with excitement and hardcore survival, No Man's Sky won't float your boat. There is a surival mode, but from my experience it often invovles hiding in shelters to warm up, walking in a frozen wasteland, hiding again, etc.

Don't worry about getting to the center, the ending will disappoint. Just worry about enjoying the journey.

I found out my graphics card is 0.5 gbs under the VRAM requirement to run the game correctly (it prefers 1.5 gbs of VRAM), but it still works at low resolutions. The game should warn you if you will have the same issue.

It's pricy. What you are getting is a well-made indie game with a techy/graphicsy sheen to it, content wise it will feel small for a pricy title.

and yeah, the game doesn't try to get you hooked, so don't expect to binge without feeling bored

Don't be put off by the massive amount of hate this game has received. It falls well short of what was promised (at the moment) but it's a good game in its own right - albeit over-priced. Recent updates have turned this game around, and work continues.

The problem is that it has now become 'cool' to hate on No Man's Sky. In the early days it probably deserved at least some of that hate. Not so much now, though there's still a lot of work to do. If I'm honest, this game should have been released as Early Access - but I presume that the deal with console manufacturers really put a stop to that. (And was likely the reason a decent amount of the promised content was missing).

Base building is fun, and now you can deploy several types of planetary vehicle, own a freighter, and farm - as well as the usual prospecting, scavenging and exploring. This is all post-release content. There's actually a crafting arc now, and it's fun... so far, anyway.

Acquisition of tech has been slowed RIGHT down. Now you actually have something to work towards. There's a lot more alien life around. Stations actually have a point to their existence now, beyond just being a pace to find the market. 

There's actually a decent amount of content, and I have hopes that this will continue to grow until the game reaches its full potential. Personally, I still think that it needs to be cheaper, but there's enough to keep you playing for a while.

The atmospheric flight model is still attrocious - though better than it was by far. You don't really have full flight control. Your ship refuses to drop below a certain altitude unless you hit the land button... in which case it lands for you. Atmospheric insertion is not at all dangerous... it doesn't matter how fast you go, you won't burn up, and you wont' crash into the surface. This is a shame. I think it would have been fun to have had to have paid at least token attention to how you landed on your new planets.

The space flight model is pretty standard stuff. W to accelerate. S to slow down, wiggle your mouse to steer. Controller support as you'd expect. Space combat is ho-hum. Not bad, but not great, either. So far it's all burn-and-turn, and a bit un-inspired. But still, not a focus of the game, so it's forgiveable.

There's a sense of busy-ness in the universe, but it's surface busy-ness only. Ships appear, and fly around, and buzz you while you're on the surface, but there's still not enough reason to engage with them. You actually CAN complete missions to protect freighters, and then liaise with the crew to purchase them, etc... but more faction stuff is needed. Hopefully it's coming.

I'd still like the ability to build your own ships, in much the same way you build your base - but at least there is far more variety in ship design than at first release. You can find or buy ships, and repair crashed ships. The repair model is a bit expensive, as you have to buy back your damaged cargo slots (not with real money) - and these are STUPIDLY over-priced, to the point where you may as well buy the ship new. I've got no issue paying for repairs, but this shouldn't be quite so much of a struggle, given how hard it can be to find the right ship for you in the first place.

Hello Games are (understandably) quiet. Their updates have been released without too much fanfare, and plenty of troubling silence beforehand. BUT, and this is a big but, they've been QUALITY updates that have added considerably to the longevity of the game. It says to me that they're at least committed to turning this game around and giving us a good chunk of what a lot of people thought the game was going to be from the outset.

I'm going to recommend the game, but I'm going to do it with some caveats.

1. Ignore the haters. This has just turned into a self-fueled hate-fest from people who just want to troll now. If you want to see what the game is actually like, look up a couple of (recent!) Let's Play videos from people who actually like the game, rather than people who are just out to hate on it.
