Edited 4/30/17: It's an okay game. In the end, it's not worth the money now that I've put...time into it. I was in denial back then. 



Hello hello! First time leaving a review so I'll try to be thourough as possible. I'm not too computer savvy when it comes to the technical side, but I'll try my best for the begining. What I'm running on (i think) is: 

Intel Core i7
8GB of RAM
Nivida GTX 970M

So far I've experienced no crashes whatsoever. Very limited frame drops when loading in bigger planets or desending into the atmosphere of one. The game runs as smoothly as one could expect it and even better than that considering it's the first day of this game's release. I didn't get any of the usual alt-tab bugs or glitches. No screen tears either. So far, so good. 


Gameplay
No Man's Sky is an exploration game more than anything. The survival is very limited and although it drops the player smack dab into the gameplay without much warning or a tutorial level, it's not difficult to connect the dots and learn how to survive. If anything, it's nearly too simplistic. In replacement of food or rest, players must find resources to recharge their essential tools such as the mining lazer and life support. Doing so, especially on the first planet, becomes easier as you become more familiar with the fauna and flora planets have to offer and how to use resource finding tools, such as the scanner. 

Going back to exploration; my goodness the game does a great job of sucking away time. The exploration in this game is an evolved emulating machine with realistic changes to the environment. I've only been to 2 planets so far ( my first one being large and my curiosity getting the better of me ) but the difference between them is like comparing night and day. Planets with high radiation eat away at life support faster, planets with extreme level conditions knock out sheilds pretty quickly and force the player to retreat into duck ins such as caves, outposts, and shelters which are spread a good, healthy distance apart to seek releif from the planets onslauts. 

However, regeneration and the threat of rampant fauna and flora ( as i've seen so far ) is minimal. Health is easy to regenerate and everything, so far, has been particularly tame. Not that it's a bad thing. Between traveling back and forth and too and fro to pick up materials or pet the cutest little generated critters, the players time is going to be eatten by emerssion. The distance and scale of everything makes  everything seem natural ( aside from the monoliths that inhabit planets ) and almost daunting. However, climbing mountains and reviewing your progress has to be the most rewarding aspect of the game. 

That is, if the texture pops don't bother you too much. For me, it's not much of an issue. It's only a game and, besides, there's gotta be a few ups and downs here and there. 

The biggest positive would have to be the aliens. Although NPC's, they bring a sort of life to the game and interaction that replaces human interaction. It's soothing and funny to be greeted by a snotting Gek or some other life form and to be taught an entirely different language. I've never been so excited to go out and hunt a practical dictionary just to communicate with the buggers i've seen. Getting so caught up in this aspect makes the lack of humans berable. As I've seen that's been the biggest complaint so far. Personally, the lack of humans being seen right away is refreshing. It gives a sense of purpose: to find someone. The build up to actually seeing and meeting someone is thrilling, especially when seeing spaceships overhead on the planets. 


Overall
To give this review a once over, I would say that NMS hit the nail on the head on an exploration game. No technical issues, or bugs here. I thuroughly enjoy what they've presented and the hype has lived up to it's grandure.

No Man's Sky is an extremely niche game. It's not a bombastic adventure through space, conquering new worlds. It's a plodding, ocassionally stunning meditation. 

What plot there is, found in anchient records and cryptic messages, is essentially a dicussion of existential purpose. It's not super unique, but it's decent, and serves to inbue the mechanics with a semblence of meaning.

The base-building mechanics and vehicles added since launch do a lot to make the game "playable," and I have no doubt HG will continue to support the game with good content.

There are many meaningful experiences to be had here, if you're open to them. There's nothing like standing on some tiny moon, looking out at half a dozen planets, and feeling tiny, only to enter the galaxy map, and find those massive worlds as specks. 

It's powerful, but not for everyone.

Reviews.219694:
Updating my review following the foundation and pathfinder updates

PROS:
- Great visuals. (UPDATE: Even better graphics now)
- Good sounds, ambiance and music.
- Exploration is so much fun, you often forget what you're supposed to be actually doing.
- Piloting your spaceship for the first time is equally exciting and terrifying.
- I got slapped by a plant. Scared the piss out of me.
- (Foundation) Base building adds a nice layer of progression to the game. The workers you hire each have quests for you to do and reward you with blueprints to further customize your base. Said customization is actually pretty decent too, you can build something unique and even share your base online.
- (Pathfinder) Weapon and ship classes. You can now buy a weapon or ship better suited for your selected playstyle. This is one of the features that was missing at launch and it's a welcomed addition to the game.
- Every update adds new functionality and general quality of life improvements, showing that Hello Games does listen to player feedback despite the problems at launch.

CONS:
- Needs to be optimized. Runs smoothly at 60 FPS on my high end computer with the occasionnal hiccup but it appears to be too demanding at the moment for the average machine. Be warned if your computer is a bit dated.
- The UI could do with some improvements, but nothing unmanageable. (UPDATE: They have been making improvements, which is good, although it still has it's share of small annoyances)
- The Inventory system is a bit frustrating, would be nice if everything could stack (and if the maximum stack numbers were increased). (UPDATE: You can now stack items in your ship.)
- (Foundation) You can't build a base wherever you like. You need to find an abandoned base and claim it as your own. This can be pretty heartbreaking when you find the perfect planet but no abandoned base on it to stake your claim.
- The faction system has been slightly improved upon with the pathfinder update but still feels hollow and unsatisfying.

I still highly recommend this game, even more so after the foundation and pathfinder updates. The fact that I keep coming back to it every update and appreciated every minute spent in-game speaks for itself. I do, however, advise any potential buyer to look into the product they are buying beforehand so as to avoid potential disappointment, this is a bit of a niche game so make sure it's the right one for you.
Reviews.219842:
So i liked this game when it first came out (although I was as upset as everyone else with all the missing features). But then I got bored, and I didnt play for a while. Since the foundation update however the game has an all new addictive component: base building and the acquisition of freighters. 

This is not a Mass Effect game on a major scale. Its not elite dangerous or space engineers or empyrion. Its NMS, and its main focus is exploration. There is no real story: just you exploring the galaxy. Yea, you can go to the center of the galaxy and follow the atlas path, but thats all secondary to just exploring new worlds. Thats the stated objective, and understanding that is key to enjoying the game. If its not your thing its not the game for you. 

All that said there is still a lot of work that can be done from creating snow planets that environmentally feel like they're covered in snow, to desert planets that look and feel like they have oceans of sand rather than just different colored textures. Actually massive mountains and deep revines would be nice too. And while the current game mechanics dont support it, running water and waterfalls would be cool. Customization is improving and the most recent update finally allows you to rename your ships, but you stil cant design your own banner/sigil/thingy or anything. Hopefully future updates (preferably more frequent smaller ones) continue to expand on what you can make your own.

But all in all there is no other game out there that has attempted what this game has done, despite its flaws. Im still convinced Hello Games was forced to release early, and their continued updates seem to suggest their passion for its success is still there. 

TL;DR If you want a chill adventure game in a beautiful universe this game is for you. Ignore the haters.

An extremely stylised game with a LOT of potential - just a shame that all the hype ruined a concept that was never going to meet its ambitions right on release date simply because it was developed by a few dozen people.

This is a 1st person exploration survival game which seems a primitive cross between Rust and Elite: Dangerous with a good measure of Spore thrown in to add to the surrealness: you play as a lone explorer with an upgradeable ship who has the freedom to climb anything and go anywhere and meet an infinite number of procedurally generated creature sprites and witness millions upon millions of worlds. If you can get past the rather copy-n-pasted look to just about everything this game has to offer, you can enjoy the spectacular terrain & landscape updates that have been churned out by Hello Games in order to keep their fanbase: and it's been worth it.
Between seeing incredible planets hanging in the sky and wild aliens dancing across colourful worlds, this game has a very fulfilling base-building system that lets you build whatever Star Trek home you could want on any beautiful world.

Looking forwards to seeing a space Rust in the future that is worth my £40 pre-order, I'm happy to let the dev team keep it simply for these guys to pursue their dreams :)
